nodes.description: External pure function compute(uint256 x) returns uint256 result; performs a degree-~130 polynomial evaluation using inline assembly mulmod/add (Horner's method) and returns result % PRIME.
Caller-supplied input parameter x of compute; the evaluation point of the polynomial, used directly inside the assembly mulmod chain without any range validation.
Local constant PRIME = 0x800000000000011000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000001, used as the modulus for every mulmod and for the final result % PRIME reduction.
Inline assembly block performing unchecked modular arithmetic (mulmod/add chain) plus the Solidity-level result % PRIME reduction; low-level arithmetic without overflow/underflow guards.

edges.reason: The parameter x is fed directly into the assembly mulmod chain as the Horner multiplier; mulmod keeps every intermediate value below PRIME, so no overflow/underflow is introduced by this flow.
PRIME is the modulus argument of every mulmod call and of the final result % PRIME reduction, so its value determines the arithmetic domain of the unsafe operation.
Execution of the compute function unconditionally enters the inline assembly arithmetic block before returning the reduced result.
The value produced by the assembly arithmetic block is reduced with result % PRIME and returned by compute as the function's result.

normalization_plan.reason: Parameter x has no independent semantic role outside compute; it exists only as the evaluation point consumed by the function's arithmetic, so it is collapsed into the compute function node.
The local PRIME constant is a fixed modulus used exclusively by the inline assembly mulmod/add chain and the final reduction, so it is absorbed into the arithmetic unsafe_operation node.
